subject: general
question:
Find the inter quartile range for the following series.
3, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Count the number of terms (n) = 11.

Q₁ (First Quartile) is the 3rd term: 6.

Q₃ (Third Quartile) is the 9th term: 18.

Inter Quartile Range (IQR) = Q₃ − Q₁ = 18 − 6 = 12.

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Series = 3, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22

**Formula Used:** Inter Quartile Range (IQR) = Q₃ − Q₁

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/00d19202765a3909bba79710c02b03ea0cd16e265b61a4480fa732e509b63b07.png] 

⇒ Total number of terms (n) = 11

⇒ Q₁ = ((n + 1) ÷ 4)th term

⇒ Q₁ = (12 ÷ 4)th term = 3rd term = 6

⇒ Q₃ = (3 × (n + 1) ÷ 4)th term

⇒ Q₃ = (3 × 12 ÷ 4)th term = 9th term = 18

⇒ IQR = 18 − 6 = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Quartile Deviation (QD)

Also known as the Semi-Interquartile Range, it is calculated as QD = (Q₃ − Q₁) ÷ 2.

Coefficient of Quartile Deviation

A relative measure of dispersion given by the formula: (Q₃ − Q₁) ÷ (Q₃ + Q₁).

Median (Q₂)

The middle value of the data set, which corresponds to the 50th percentile or the ((n + 1) ÷ 2)th term.</p
